evidence: Sitewide project CTAs now use /contact/?inquiry=project#inquiry-paths and free-review CTAs use /contact/?inquiry=review#inquiry-paths. assets/js/site.js reads the allowed inquiry value and progressively selects the matching project or review radio option. The homepage retains a review fallback and /contact/ retains a project fallback when no valid intent is supplied.
impact: A visitor who explicitly chose Start a Project lands in a different conversion path and must correct the form, creating friction at the highest-value step.
recommended_fix: Route project CTAs to /contact/?inquiry=project#inquiry-paths, route free-review CTAs with inquiry=review, and progressively select the matching radio option.
validation_method: Source/CTA invariant check plus local Chromium navigation and DOM-state checks for inquiry=project and inquiry=review; no production form submission was made.
remaining_risk: Invalid or missing intent values use each page's documented fallback; future campaign and external links must preserve one of the allowed values.

evidence: The no-cost route is now consistently named Free Initial Review across primary CTA and form copy. The paid service remains Audits & Advisory and uses the distinct Discuss an In-Depth Audit CTA. A case-insensitive visible-copy inventory found no legacy Free Website, Email, Brand, Automation, or generic Audit offer variants.
impact: Visitors may not understand the difference between a preliminary email review and a paid, scoped audit.
recommended_fix: Use one no-cost offer name and descriptor, and give the paid audit page a distinct primary CTA for an in-depth scoped engagement.
validation_method: Case-insensitive terminology inventory across visible HTML plus manual review of free-review and paid-audit CTA destinations.
remaining_risk: The owner must ensure the response actually delivered for each offer remains consistent with the published distinction.

evidence: Partial static mitigation is present: /pricing/ tells visitors to contact RielArt before ordering when scope, platform, integrations, content, access, or timing is unclear; it also states scope, separate-cost, billing, and onboarding expectations. The final static audit confirms all 6 approved Stripe links, but repository source cannot verify account-level product, price/cadence, tax, agreement, refund/cancellation, success/cancel, or post-payment settings.
impact: A buyer could purchase before important scope or policy expectations are mutually clear.
recommended_fix: Add a concise contact-before-order safeguard in static copy and have the owner verify every Stripe product, agreement, and post-payment flow.
validation_method: Static safeguard and 6-of-6 approved-link audit completed; owner-observed Stripe product, checkout, agreement, and post-payment review remains outstanding, without completing a charge.
remaining_risk: Account-level configuration and the end-to-end customer experience cannot be validated from this repository.

evidence: Both forms retain native validation and a live status region. Capture-phase invalid handling now sets aria-invalid=true and announces Please review the highlighted required fields; input/change handling clears the state when the control or required radio group becomes valid.
impact: Some assistive-technology users may receive less clear feedback about why submission did not proceed.
recommended_fix: On invalid events set aria-invalid, announce a concise review message in the existing live region, and clear the state when a control becomes valid.
validation_method: Source review plus local Chromium keyboard/empty-submit, DOM-state, and live-region text checks without a Formspree submission.
remaining_risk: Announcement behavior still requires verification with real assistive technology such as NVDA and VoiceOver.

evidence: images/logo.png is now an optimized 128 x 128 PNG of 8,587 bytes, reduced from the 512 x 512, 92,374-byte baseline while retaining the same sitewide asset path.
impact: Every first-time page visit transfers avoidable image bytes, affecting mobile performance and cache footprint.
recommended_fix: Resize the source to a high-density 128×128 optimized PNG while visually verifying the mark at rendered size.
validation_method: PNG header inspection and byte-size comparison plus light/dark rendered-size visual review.
remaining_risk: A separate higher-resolution source would be needed if the mark is used substantially larger in the future.

evidence: Both below-the-fold person photos on /about/ now declare loading=lazy and decoding=async while retaining explicit width, height, and alt attributes.
impact: They can compete with above-the-fold work on the first load even when the user does not scroll to the team section.
recommended_fix: Add loading=lazy and decoding=async while preserving explicit dimensions and alt text.
validation_method: Two-of-two source-attribute check plus browser visual review.
remaining_risk: Browser scheduling is implementation-dependent.

evidence: Materially changed primary non-article routes now use 2026-07-27 lastmod values. Existing article dates remain 2026-07-18 or 2026-07-12, and the unchanged terms route remains 2026-07-12.
impact: The sitemap does not accurately communicate the modification date of substantive page changes.
recommended_fix: Update lastmod only for materially changed non-article pages and leave unchanged article dates intact.
validation_method: Final audit parsed all 25 sitemap URLs and 25 ISO lastmod values, verified indexable-route parity, and reported 0 warnings and 0 critical failures.
remaining_risk: Future edits require a maintained lastmod workflow.

evidence: Production GitHub Pages returns HTTP 200 for the legacy documents; their HTML contains noindex/canonical/redirect behavior, but the repository _redirects file is not applied by this host.
impact: Browsers and crawlers receive a client-side redirect document instead of a clean server-side 301.
recommended_fix: Preserve the compatibility documents now; configure edge/server redirects if hosting gains that capability.
validation_method: Production HTTP status and Location-header checks plus source inspection.
remaining_risk: Cannot be fully corrected in a standard GitHub Pages repository.

evidence: The homepage Twitter description now uses the rebuilt core promise, Build a stronger brand, create a clearer website, and run a smarter business with RielArt, aligned with the Open Graph description apart from its deliberate brand suffix. The Process document title is now the specific Our Digital Project Process | RielArt.
impact: Accurate, distinctive metadata helps visitors and crawlers understand each page and reduces mismatches in search results and social previews.
recommended_fix: Keep the homepage social description synchronized with its current promise and retain a concise, descriptive, unique title for the Process page.
validation_method: Direct head-metadata comparison plus sitewide title and description uniqueness checks in the reusable static audit.
remaining_risk: Search engines and social platforms may rewrite or cache metadata; rendered previews should be checked after deployment.

evidence: Production responses include HTTPS and HSTS but did not expose CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame protection, or cross-origin policy headers.
impact: The site lacks several browser defense-in-depth controls despite having a small static attack surface.
recommended_fix: Document required domains and deploy a report-only CSP followed by staged enforcement at a configurable host/CDN; add compatible security headers there.
validation_method: Production response-header inspection and CSP violation monitoring after a hosting change.
remaining_risk: GitHub Pages does not provide repository-level arbitrary response-header configuration; a restrictive meta policy could break inline theme code or external flows.

evidence: The privacy policy's service-provider disclosure now names Calendly for optional consultation scheduling alongside Formspree, Cloudflare, Resend, and Stripe, and states that the external service applies its own processing terms.
impact: The implementation-to-policy inventory is incomplete for visitors who choose external scheduling.
recommended_fix: Add a factual technical disclosure that optional scheduling opens Calendly and is subject to its processing, without making new legal conclusions.
validation_method: Sitewide external-service/link inventory and source-level privacy-policy consistency review.
remaining_risk: Counsel/owner must approve legal adequacy and international-processing wording.

evidence: The unsupported Advertising filter has been removed. Every remaining blog filter maps to at least one article-card category: Brand, Web & UX, AI & Automation, SEO & Analytics, or Operations.
impact: Selecting it creates an avoidable empty state and implies content coverage that is not present.
recommended_fix: Remove the filter until a substantive advertising article exists.
validation_method: Filter-to-card taxonomy inventory plus local Chromium interaction and visible-result-count checks.
remaining_risk: The filter should be restored only when matching content is published.

evidence: All four interactive homepage priority panels now label their final field Intended outcome.
impact: The label can sound more certain than an intended, non-guaranteed outcome.
recommended_fix: Use Intended outcome.
validation_method: Four-of-four visible-copy source check plus local Chromium rendered-text inspection.
remaining_risk: Outcome statements still need to avoid unsupported guarantees.

evidence: The required email field on both the homepage and contact page is now labelled Email while retaining type=email and autocomplete=email.
impact: Solo operators or buyers using a general business mailbox may incorrectly assume their address is not acceptable.
recommended_fix: Use Email while retaining type=email and autocomplete=email.
validation_method: Visible label inspection and form-control association check.
remaining_risk: Low.

evidence: All nine articles now include a visible linked Gabriel Macovei byline that matches the JSON-LD author, a topic-specific related RielArt service block, an Explore the Service link, and a Free Initial Review CTA using inquiry=review.
impact: Attributable authorship and relevant next steps strengthen article credibility and reduce conversion dead ends.
recommended_fix: Retain linked visible bylines and topic-specific service/review CTAs as the article library grows.
validation_method: Nine-of-nine source inventory, JSON-LD author comparison, and internal target/fragment audit.
remaining_risk: Author identity and biographical claims still depend on owner accuracy; CTA effectiveness requires privacy-aware measurement.

affected_url: /; /services/ and all five service detail routes; /about/; /faq/; /portfolio/; /thanks/
affected_file: index.html; services/index.html; services/*/index.html; about/index.html; faq/index.html; portfolio/index.html; thanks/index.html
evidence: The baseline HTML repeated the modifiers practical 127 times, constraint 18 times, and useful next step 4 times across source and repeated metadata/footer content. A restrained buyer-facing pass made 51 exact phrase edits across 11 files; the final inventory is 87, 11, and 0 respectively while Practical AI remains where it identifies the established offer.
impact: Repeated abstract modifiers can make otherwise concrete service copy feel templated or AI-generated and weaken scanability.
recommended_fix: Replace only generic repeated phrases with specific buyer language while preserving accurate technical uses and the established Practical AI descriptor.
validation_method: Before/after case-insensitive phrase inventory, targeted diff review, static audit, and responsive browser regression on representative commercial pages.
remaining_risk: Editorial judgment remains subjective; future copy should prioritize concrete nouns and actions without mechanically banning useful terms.

affected_url: Brand, AI Automation, Digital Growth, and Audits service pages
evidence: Brand, AI Automation, Digital Growth, and Audits service pages now state the specific factors controlling timing or cadence, including scope, access, source material, feedback/approvals, integration/data complexity, selected allowance, priorities, analytics, and third-party dependencies as applicable.
impact: Prospective clients have less help forming realistic schedule expectations.
recommended_fix: Add one concise, non-promissory timing statement using only visible dependencies already described by each service.
validation_method: Five-service content matrix confirming a concise dependency-based timing statement on every detailed service page, followed by manual non-promissory claims review.
remaining_risk: Exact durations remain scope-dependent and should not be invented.

evidence: All nine Article JSON-LD documents now include articleSection mapped to the visible taxonomy: Brand, Web & UX, AI & Automation, SEO & Analytics, or Operations. Blog-index structured entries use the same mapping.
impact: Machine-readable categorization is less consistent than the visible information architecture.
recommended_fix: Map articleSection values to Brand, Web & UX, AI & Automation, SEO & Analytics, or Operations where the category is visibly supported.
validation_method: Parsed all 35 JSON-LD blocks and compared nine-of-nine articleSection values with the visible article taxonomy; the final audit reported no structured-data warning.
remaining_risk: Schema improvements do not guarantee search-result features.

evidence: The tracked tools/__pycache__/site_audit.cpython-312.pyc artifact has been removed from the working tree. .gitignore now excludes __pycache__/ and *.py[cod], and deployment configuration excludes the tools directory.
impact: It adds irrelevant binary noise, interpreter-specific churn, and an unnecessary deployable artifact.
recommended_fix: Remove the exact tracked cache file and ignore __pycache__ and Python bytecode.
validation_method: Working-tree deletion check, Git ignore-rule check for Python cache output, and deployment-exclusion audit.
remaining_risk: The deletion and ignore/exclusion changes must be committed and published; unrelated future generated artifacts still need review.

evidence: _config.yml defines 17 deployment-exclusion rules covering audit reports, internal artifacts, and tools. The reusable audit checks local and social assets, metadata, headings, JSON-LD, forms, sitemap dates, redirects, placeholders/disclosures, legal references, approved Stripe links, and build artifacts. The final run found all 17 present internal artifact paths safely excluded.
impact: Internal working files stay out of the published site and repeatable checks make regressions easier to detect before deployment.
recommended_fix: Keep the exclusion list and reusable audit aligned with repository structure, and run the audit before each release.
validation_method: Bundled-Python audit completed with exit code 0 across 30 HTML files, 25 indexable routes, 241 asset references, 35 JSON-LD blocks, 2 forms, and 4 redirects, with 0 warnings and 0 critical failures.
remaining_risk: The deployment must actually build with _config.yml; exclusions and audit coverage need revision whenever files or the publishing pipeline change.

evidence: The page honestly labels its content as illustrative service models rather than client case studies, but the navigation label Work and H1 can still imply completed client proof.
impact: A visitor expecting case studies may perceive a proof gap even though the disclosure prevents a false claim.
recommended_fix: Owner decision: add one approved, attributable real case study when available or rename the route label/title to Solution Examples.
validation_method: Owner approval and subsequent content/claims review.
remaining_risk: No testimonial, client, or outcome may be invented to close this gap.

evidence: Daniel Patel is displayed with a photograph and role/relationship wording that cannot be independently verified from repository content.
impact: Incorrect or unapproved people information would create a credibility and consent risk.
recommended_fix: Confirm identity, current role, relationship wording, photo rights, and consent with the business owner.
validation_method: Owner and subject confirmation.
remaining_risk: Static QA cannot prove permission or employment/contract status.

evidence: Repository review cannot determine whether refund, cancellation, recurring billing, governing law, international processing, AI, portfolio, advertising, and agreement language exactly matches business practice and third-party account settings.
impact: Policy/site/account inconsistencies can create customer confusion and legal exposure.
recommended_fix: Have the owner and qualified counsel review the policies after technical changes and record effective dates and account-level decisions.
validation_method: Owner/counsel review against actual operations and provider settings.
remaining_risk: This audit is a technical consistency review, not legal advice.

evidence: No analytics or advertising measurement platform was found in the repository.
impact: RielArt cannot reliably quantify CTA, form, scheduling, pricing, portal, or article-to-service performance from site code alone.
recommended_fix: Approve a privacy-aware platform and consent approach before installing one; use a single event layer and never send form contents or personal data.
validation_method: Owner approval, implementation review, debug-mode event testing, and privacy-policy update.
remaining_risk: Consent and disclosure needs vary by audience, jurisdiction, and selected vendor.

evidence: Static checks confirm the expected endpoints and links but cannot prove Formspree delivery/spam handling, Stripe product details, or checkout/post-payment behavior without controlled account access and side effects.
impact: A syntactically correct link can still lead to a misconfigured external workflow.
recommended_fix: Run owner-controlled test submissions and checkout reviews, clearly labelled as tests, then document receipt, routing, agreement, and follow-up.
validation_method: Authorized account-level test and recorded evidence.
remaining_risk: Automated production submissions were intentionally avoided.

evidence: Chromium viewport emulation has covered 320, 360, 390, 430, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920, and 2560 CSS pixels. Current real-engine/device coverage for Firefox, Safari/macOS, iOS Safari, and Android Chrome remains unavailable, as do NVDA/VoiceOver verification, 200/400% zoom, text-spacing, high-contrast, and current Lighthouse/axe or field Core Web Vitals evidence.
impact: Engine- and assistive-technology-specific defects can remain after strong automated and Chromium coverage.
recommended_fix: Complete owner-approved BrowserStack or real-device checks for current Safari, iOS Safari, Android Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and at least one screen reader.
validation_method: Completed Chromium viewport matrix plus an outstanding manual real-browser/device/assistive-technology matrix with screenshots and issue notes; run Lighthouse and axe when those tools/environments are available.
remaining_risk: Viewport emulation is not equivalent to real device or engine testing, and no current lab accessibility/performance score, screen-reader result, or field INP/Core Web Vitals dataset is available.
